conclusion: The existing covariance_matrix kernel is correctness-first (one thread per matrix cell, no parallel reduction) and remains PARITY-VALIDATED (<= 4.91e-11). At the candidate-set sizes that can actually enter a portfolio (<= a few hundred names), optimized numpy/BLAS covariance is faster than this kernel across all tested sizes, so covariance stays on CPU per the measured crossover policy. A tiled/threadgroup-reduction covariance kernel is the documented optimization path; it is deferred because it would not change the operational decision at realistic candidate-set sizes. The kernel is retained, consumed (M3), and parity-validated.
decision: CPU covariance for realistic candidate sets; GPU kernel retained + parity-validated; tiled kernel documented as measured-justified deferral.
